Seed-paired policy comparison

Source: R/result.R
compare_policies.Rd

Because every policy runs replicate r from the same random number stream (see run_experiment()), per-replicate differences between policies are paired. Pairing removes between-replicate noise from the comparison, exactly as paired seeds do in a designed simulation study.

Usage

compare_policies(
  result,
  metric = c("cumulative_regret", "total_reward"),
  baseline = NULL
)

Arguments

result

A bandit_result with at least two policies and at least two replications.

metric

"cumulative_regret" (default) or "total_reward".

baseline

Name of the baseline policy. Default: the first policy in the experiment.

Value

A tibble with one row per non-baseline policy and replicate: policy, baseline, replicate, the metric under each, and difference (policy minus baseline). For cumulative_regret, negative differences favour the policy; for total_reward, positive differences favour the policy.

Examples

env <- bandit_bernoulli(c(a = 0.2, b = 0.5))
result <- run_experiment(
  env,
  list(epsilon = policy_epsilon_greedy(0.1), ucb = policy_ucb1()),
  horizon = 300, replications = 20, seed = 7
)
comparison <- compare_policies(result, baseline = "epsilon")
aggregate(difference ~ policy, data = comparison, FUN = mean)
#>   policy difference
#> 1    ucb      3.015
